newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia, Syria agree to expand trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia, Syria agree to expand trade.

text.p: Syrian Prime Minister Mahmoud Zu'bi and Indonesia's President Suharto agreed to expand economic relations and trade between the two countries, Indonesian State Secretary Murdiono said Friday.

"Both leaders agreed on the need to expand economic relations and to boost trade between the two countries," Murdiono told reporters after talks between Suharto and Zu'bi, who is on a four-day official visit.
"The two countries also agreed to encourage their private sectors to take a bigger role in expanding the economy," he said.
In the political field, Murdiono said Indonesia, the world's most populous Moslem state,supported the Arab struggle to regain areas occupied by Israel.
"President Suharto stated full support for the struggle of Arab nations, especially Syria, to get back their land occupied by Israel," Murdiono said.
"Indonesia will not consider opening diplomatic ties with Israel so long as Israel fails to fulfill United Nation's resolutions, especially the return of Arab land," he said.

Murdiono said Syria fully supported Jakarta over East Timor, a former Portuguese colony invaded by Indonesia in 1975 and incorporated as the country's 27th province the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
Zu'bi arrived in Jakarta on Thursday and will leave for home early on Monday.
